1900: Choiseul, Ysabel, Shortland and Fauro join the protectorate: they 'were transferred to the United Kingdom under the Samoa Tripartite Convention of 1899' (infobox 'Tripartite Convention: 14 November 1899'); 'In October 1900, the High Commissioner issued a Proclamation extending the Protectorate to the islands in question'.

region.text: the Solomon Islands, invaded by Japan in January 1942

ledger.note: 1942: the Japanese invade the Solomon Islands (January 1942): 'after the Japanese invasion of the Solomon Islands in January 1942'; the Guadalcanal campaign page: they 'had occupied Tulagi in May 1942'. Which islands the Japanese held is not on the pages opened; the whole protectorate is the researcher's bridging reading (confidence 1). The reviewer should read this pair as a gap rather than a fact.
1942: the Guadalcanal campaign: 'On 7 August 1942, Allied forces, predominantly U.S. Marines, landed on Guadalcanal, Tulagi, and Florida Island'.

1943: the Guadalcanal campaign ends: 'It was fought between 7 August 1942 and 9 February 1943'; the Japanese 'evacuated their last forces by 9 February 1943'. The Allies hold Guadalcanal, Tulagi and Florida; the occupation of the remaining islands goes on.
1945: the Japanese military administration ends (the page's infobox lists a Japanese Military Administration 1941-1945; no day or surrender is on the pages opened).

wars.name: Guadalcanal campaign
wars.outcome: Allied landings on 7 August 1942; the Japanese 'evacuated their last forces by 9 February 1943'. 'Guadalcanal, British Solomon Islands' (the page's location).
wars.note: The page dates the Japanese occupation of Tulagi to May 1942.

certainty.note: The protectorate's limits are 'the southern Solomon Islands'; the line with the German islands (Choiseul, Ysabel, Shortland, Fauro) is not on the page and the islands are named, not bounded.
Fixed by the Tripartite Convention (14 November 1899) and the October 1900 Proclamation; an island group whose border is the sea and the Bougainville Strait.

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. Pages used: British Solomon Islands, Guadalcanal campaign. The shape is the modern Solomon Islands country; the province split of 1893 to 1899 is the researcher's reading of the page's island lists.
WHAT THE PAGES DO NOT HAVE. The 6 October 1893 date (the page says June 1893); the Ontong Java and Sikaiana limits; the Anglo-German line; any area; Japan's surrender; the Japanese hold on individual islands. The occupation_start/end pair of 1942-1945 is therefore confidence 1: the empire-of-japan dossier (jk-01) records a Solomon Islands occupation with counterpart british-colonial-empire and should use this slug. Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire row (eu-11) still draws 78 cells of the Solomons in 1980 (oc-02-b), which should end in 1978.
The page budget (two pages) was used for the protectorate and the Guadalcanal campaign; the Solomon Islands campaign beyond Guadalcanal (New Georgia, Bougainville) is not entered. oc-02-b's solomon-islands dossier starts at independence.
